sources.title: Environmental and Social Management Framework: Resilient Urban and Territorial Development Project (RUTDP), Volume 1: Main Report
sources.organization: Local Government Engineering Department, Government of Bangladesh
sources.temporal_coverage: Project context in 2024; first project phase planned for 2024-2030.
sources.methodology: Government project ESMF based primarily on the feasibility study and available secondary data.
sources.limitations: Subproject locations and designs were not finalized at preparation; the framework does not report completed outcomes.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Bangladesh Background Note, Environment, Natural Resources and Blue Economy
geographic_coverage: Chittagong Hill Forests in the east
sources.temporal_coverage: Bangladesh CCDR 2022 background note drawing on studies published in different years.
sources.methodology: CCDR background note synthesizing cited studies on ecosystems, coastal hazards, forests, and livelihoods.
sources.limitations: Evidence combines referenced studies with different dates and methods; this note is not a new field survey.

sources.title: Water and Health: Impact of Climate Change in Bangladesh
sources.organization: World Bank Group, Health, Nutrition, and Population Global Practice
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical studies summarized in a September 2022 discussion paper.
sources.methodology: Summarizes water and health studies by the six ecological zones used in the government Delta Plan 2100.
sources.limitations: The paper describes findings from prior studies and identifies zone-level differences; it is not a new epidemiological survey.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed pp. iii-iv (PDF pp. 3-4).
claims.paraphrase: The project ESMF describes northwest urban clusters 1 and 2 as relatively drought-prone, with less rainfall and higher temperatures than other parts of Bangladesh.
claims.limitations: Project-area characterization; not a national hazard estimate.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed p. iv (PDF p. 4).
claims.paraphrase: Coastal districts in southwest clusters 3 and 5 are described as vulnerable to salinity intrusion, cyclones, and tidal water surges.
claims.limitations: The source identifies project clusters but does not quantify hazard frequency or losses.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed pp. iii-iv (PDF pp. 3-4).
claims.paraphrase: RUTDP plans climate-resilient urban services and stronger city management across 87 municipalities and city corporations in 36 districts, targeting about 21 million people, half of them women.
claims.limitations: These are project objectives and beneficiary estimates, not evidence of completed resilience outcomes.

claims.locator: Section 1, Bangladesh Context and Problem Statement, printed p. 3 (PDF p. 2).
claims.paraphrase: The note reports that climate change, pollution, resource overuse, and rapid urbanization are degrading ecosystems and increasing livelihood threats, especially for the rural poor.
claims.limitations: The note names several concurrent pressures, so the passage does not isolate climate change as the sole driver.

claims.locator: Section 1, coastal hazard discussion, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 3).
claims.paraphrase: The note describes low-lying delta populations as exposed to cyclones and storm surges, with coastal erosion and seawater intrusion affecting land and groundwater.
claims.limitations: The note summarizes cited studies and does not provide a new spatial risk model.

claims.locator: Section 1, mangrove protection discussion, printed p. 4 (PDF p. 3).
claims.paraphrase: Studies cited by the note estimate mangroves protect 1.1-3.5 million people from cyclone flooding; villages with mangroves had about half the monetary losses of other villages during Cyclone Sidr.
claims.limitations: These are estimates attributed to cited studies, including a historical Sidr comparison, not a new causal evaluation.

claims.locator: Abstract, printed p. ii (PDF p. 4).
claims.paraphrase: The paper says Bangladesh's Delta Plan 2100 divides 64 districts into six ecological zones and identifies 58 districts as extremely vulnerable to climate change.
claims.limitations: This is the paper's summary of the government plan's classification, not an independent district assessment.

claims.locator: Abstract, printed p. ii (PDF p. 4).
claims.paraphrase: The paper reports regional health differences: groundwater depletion in Barind and drought-prone areas, saline drinking water on the coast, and especially pronounced effects for pregnant women and children.
claims.limitations: The abstract summarizes zone-level findings from earlier studies and does not estimate individual causal effects.

access_audit.locator: 142-page ESMF; Executive Summary and project context sections inspected.
access_audit.notes: Government-authored project framework opened as a complete PDF.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No reuse license established from inspected pages; no passages copied.

access_audit.notes: Full PDF opened; claims are attributed to the note and its cited literature.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Not stated in inspected pages; no passages copied.

access_audit.notes: Full PDF opened; the abstract summarizes six Delta Plan zones.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Paper permits noncommercial reproduction with attribution; no Creative Commons license stated.

access_audit.locator: Resource page and linked PDF viewer.
access_audit.notes: ADB page provides a summary, but its linked government NDC text did not open; excluded from claims.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Not inspected.

The inspected NDC search reached an ADB summary and an inaccessible viewer; the underlying NDC was excluded rather than treated as verified government text.

sources.title: Bhutan Second Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.temporal_coverage: Second NDC covering 2021-2030.
sources.methodology: Government NDC describing national climate context, institutions, and planned mitigation and adaptation actions.
sources.limitations: Policy submission; planned actions are not evaluated outcomes, and the inspected passages do not quantify local hazard exposure.

sources.title: Assessment of Climate-Induced Loss and Damage in Bhutan
sources.temporal_coverage: Assessment published in 2026; includes a documented October 2025 extreme-weather event.
sources.methodology: Review of secondary documents, key-informant group interviews, stakeholder workshop, and field visits.
sources.limitations: The report notes limited primary datasets and dispersed institutional knowledge; the inspected 2025 event passage reports impacts but does not attribute the event to climate change.

sources.title: Adaptation, Climate Resilience, and Diversification Key to Creating Jobs, Accelerating Growth in Bhutan
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank publication page dated 2025; reports modeled risks through 2050.
sources.methodology: Official World Bank release summarizing findings and recommendations from its Bhutan Country Climate and Development Report.
sources.limitations: The press-release summary does not provide underlying model specifications; the qualitative hotter-and-drier scenario is not assigned a named pathway.

claims.locator: National context, printed p. 2 (PDF p. 2).
claims.paraphrase: Bhutan's mountainous setting, reliance on hydropower and agriculture, and limited resources and capacity shape its climate vulnerability.
claims.limitations: National context statement in a government NDC; no subnational comparison is provided in this passage.

claims.locator: National climate response and 12th Five-Year Plan discussion, printed pp. 3-4 (PDF pp. 3-4).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC reports that the 12th Five-Year Plan includes climate resilience and disaster preparedness priorities and describes national coordination arrangements for climate action.
claims.limitations: The NDC describes policy arrangements and priorities, not implementation performance.

claims.locator: Assessment summary, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 10).
claims.paraphrase: The assessment identifies glacial lake outburst floods, flash floods, landslides, forest fires, and windstorms alongside slower-onset glacial retreat and ecosystem degradation, with implications for water, food, energy, infrastructure, health, and livelihoods.
claims.limitations: This is a national assessment summary; the passage does not quantify exposure by district.

claims.locator: October 2025 event case study, printed p. 79 (PDF p. 92).
claims.paraphrase: The report records heavy rain on 4-5 October 2025 followed by flash floods, landslides, swollen rivers, and windstorms; it notes crop, livestock, home, cultural-site, infrastructure, and hydropower impacts, one death, and two people missing, with Samtse, Chukha, Haa, and Dagana among the most affected districts.
claims.limitations: The report documents event impacts but this passage does not assess climate attribution.

claims.locator: Climate risk and economic impact summary, webpage paragraphs on climate scenarios and projected losses (accessed 2026-10-26).
claims.paraphrase: The World Bank release says hotter and drier conditions could affect hydropower, tourism, and agriculture and produce economic losses by 2050; it reports that adaptation and diversification could reduce projected losses by at least 40 percent.
claims.scenario: Hotter-and-drier scenario described in the official summary; no named model pathway is specified there.
claims.limitations: The official press-release summary does not disclose the modeling assumptions or define the scenario pathway.

claims.locator: Climate risks for communities and locations, webpage paragraphs on population and subnational exposure (accessed 2026-10-26).
claims.paraphrase: The release reports that about 65 percent of Bhutan's population is exposed to at least one natural hazard and identifies Zhemgang and Mongar among districts with higher risk; floods, landslides, and heat disproportionately affect vulnerable people.
claims.limitations: The release is a summary and does not present the underlying district risk method or hazard-specific population estimates.

access_audit.notes: Complete government submission PDF opened.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No reuse license identified in inspected pages; no text copied.

access_audit.notes: The publisher page, not the full underlying CCDR, was inspected.
access_audit.reuse_terms: No reuse terms inspected; no text copied.

The World Bank page is an official summary; the underlying CCDR modeling details and named scenario pathways were not inspected.

sources.title: Key Highlights: Maldives Country Climate and Development Report
sources.temporal_coverage: World Bank CCDR highlights updated 2024; includes projections to mid-century and 2100.
sources.methodology: Official World Bank summary of the Maldives CCDR findings and recommendations.
sources.limitations: The linked full CCDR PDF returned 403; claims are limited to passages on the official highlights page.

sources.title: Maldives Country Environmental Analysis: Towards a More Sustainable and Resilient Blue Economy
sources.temporal_coverage: Country Environmental Analysis published in 2024; includes current environmental analysis and prospective policy recommendations.
sources.methodology: Official World Bank page presenting CEA findings and recommendations on natural resource management and the blue economy.
sources.limitations: The linked full PDF could not be retrieved by the browser; only the substantive official publisher summary was used.

sources.title: Maldives' Third Nationally Determined Contribution: National Climate Action Plan Towards Resilience and Low-Carbon Development
sources.organization: Ministry of Tourism and Environment, Government of Maldives
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC3 submitted in February 2025; national climate assessment and action planning to 2035.
sources.methodology: Government NDC presenting climate context, consultation, adaptation priorities, and planned mitigation and resilience actions.
sources.limitations: The NDC is a policy submission, not an evaluation of outcomes; the inspected passages identify risks but do not provide island-level estimates.

claims.locator: Key findings, lines on economic reliance and climate risk (accessed 2026-10-26).
claims.paraphrase: Tourism and fisheries account for nearly half of Maldives GDP and employment; reef and fishery climate impacts are evident and projected to worsen by mid-century.
claims.scenario: Moderate/high emissions scenarios, per summary.
claims.limitations: Official highlights summarize the CCDR; full report inaccessible.

claims.locator: Key findings, sea-level-rise projection, lines 11-16 (accessed 2026-10-26).
claims.paraphrase: The summary projects 0.5–0.9 m sea-level rise by 2100; 10-year floods could damage up to 3.3% of assets (US$0.7–1.1bn).
claims.scenario: The highlights page does not specify scenarios for the sea-level or flood estimates.
claims.limitations: Model details are not provided on the highlights page.

claims.locator: Key findings, coral reef degradation and recommendations, lines 15-24 (accessed 2026-10-26).
claims.paraphrase: The summary says nearly all shallow coral cover could be lost if global temperatures exceed 2°C and recommends island-specific planning that incorporates sea-level rise, flooding, and ocean heating.
claims.scenario: Coral projection assumes global warming above 2°C.
claims.limitations: The highlights page does not provide coral-model methods.

claims.locator: CEA recommendations, institutional capacity and local council recommendations, webpage paragraphs 26-50 (accessed 2026-10-26).
claims.paraphrase: The CEA recommends strengthening environmental agency capacity and empowering island and atoll councils to manage protected areas and participate in monitoring.
claims.limitations: Recommendations indicate proposed capacity needs, not verified implementation or results.

claims.locator: Climate vulnerability and national circumstances, printed pp. 5-8 (PDF pp. 4-7).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC describes the country's low-lying narrow islands as exposed to sea-level rise and increasingly unpredictable rainfall and extreme weather, with risks to infrastructure, ecosystems, food and water security, and livelihoods.
claims.limitations: National-level context from the NDC; no island-specific risk figures are given in the cited pages.

claims.locator: Climate vulnerability and social inclusion discussion, printed pp. 6-8 (PDF pp. 5-7).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC identifies exposure of public utilities, health services, transport, and telecommunications and says climate action should address the needs of women, youth, and other vulnerable groups.
claims.limitations: The NDC identifies sectors and groups but does not quantify differentiated impacts in this passage.

sources.title: Climate Risks, Exposure, Vulnerability and Resilience in Nepal
sources.temporal_coverage: Assessment published in 2023; combines current risk mapping and mid-century climate projections.
sources.methodology: Spatial hazard maps combined with socioeconomic vulnerability indicators and CMIP6 projections.
sources.limitations: Household coping and shock outcomes are only partly captured; results are modeled.

sources.title: Second Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.organization: Government of Nepal, Ministry of Forests and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC covering 2021-2030.
sources.methodology: Government submission setting out national climate vulnerability context and adaptation priorities.
sources.limitations: The NDC is a policy statement and planned response, not an evaluation of implementation outcomes.

sources.title: Synopsis of Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0
sources.organization: Government of Nepal, Ministry of Forests and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: NDC 3.0 synopsis setting out priorities through 2035.
sources.methodology: Four-page government synopsis of climate commitments, adaptation priorities, and estimated investment needs.
sources.limitations: Brief synopsis rather than a full technical assessment; proposed investment needs and plans are not achieved results.

claims.locator: Agriculture and socioeconomic vulnerability, printed pp. 9-10 (PDF pp. 8-9).
claims.paraphrase: With 62% of workers in agriculture, Terai rainfed smallholders face floods; limited safety nets constrain coping.
claims.limitations: Household losses are not quantified.

claims.locator: Hazard selection and spatial mapping, printed pp. 25-27 (PDF p. 26).
claims.paraphrase: Hazard maps place greatest river-flood risk along Nepal’s southern border and valleys, plus heat, drought, landslide, and air pollution.
claims.limitations: Maps estimate hazard, not losses.

claims.locator: Heat stress exposure, printed p. 30 (PDF p. 30).
claims.paraphrase: Over 4.3 million people fall in the extreme heat-stress category for a modeled 20-year event, concentrated in southern municipalities.
claims.scenario: Modeled 20-year heat-stress event; the passage is an exposure estimate, not a climate projection.
claims.limitations: Modeled exposure, not illness counts.

claims.locator: CMIP6 precipitation projections, printed pp. 50-59 (PDF pp. 52-58).
claims.paraphrase: Mid-century CMIP6 projections show larger extreme-precipitation changes in western Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim than farther east.
claims.scenario: CMIP6 SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5.
claims.limitations: Regional model comparison; uncertainty remains.

claims.locator: Drought and temperature projections, printed pp. 50-59 (PDF pp. 52-58).
claims.paraphrase: The report projects persistent western drought and rising heat nationwide, with stronger warming under SSP5-8.5.
claims.scenario: CMIP6 SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, and SSP5-8.5; stronger warming is reported under SSP5-8.5.
claims.limitations: Modeled projections, not observed outcomes.

claims.locator: National vulnerability statement, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 1).
claims.paraphrase: Nepal's Second NDC describes the country as vulnerable because of fragile topography, climate-sensitive livelihoods, and limited adaptive capacity.
claims.limitations: This is the government's national framing in its 2020 NDC, not a comparative fragility classification.

claims.locator: Adaptation priorities, printed p. 17 (PDF p. 17).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC sets adaptation priorities across agriculture and food security, forests and watersheds, water and energy, settlements, infrastructure, tourism and heritage, health, and disaster risk reduction.
claims.limitations: These are stated priorities for 2021-2030, not evaluated implementation results.

claims.locator: Adaptation investment needs in the four-page NDC 3.0 synopsis (PDF pp. 2-3).
claims.paraphrase: The government synopsis estimates US$18-20 billion for adaptation priorities through 2035 and identifies grants as a financing need for adaptation and loss-and-damage actions.
claims.limitations: This is an estimated investment need in a short government synopsis, not a secured or spent amount.

claims.locator: Planned data and displacement measures in the NDC 3.0 synopsis (PDF pp. 2-3).
claims.paraphrase: The synopsis identifies plans to strengthen data systems for slow- and rapid-onset events and to develop planning for climate-induced displacement and resettlement.
claims.limitations: These are proposed actions in a synopsis; implementation and results were not assessed.

access_audit.notes: Full PDF opened; report includes mapped exposure and CMIP6 projections.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Report states Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 IGO license; attribution required.

access_audit.notes: Complete government submission opened.

sources.title: Sri Lanka: Systematic Country Diagnostic Update
sources.temporal_coverage: Diagnostic published January 2022; includes reported historical disaster losses and climate risk context.
sources.methodology: Diagnostic update synthesizing newer analysis, prior studies, and stakeholder consultations.
sources.limitations: Synthesizes studies of varying dates and methods; not a new attribution study.

sources.title: Nationally Determined Contributions Implementation Plan (2021-2030)
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment, Government of Sri Lanka
sources.temporal_coverage: Published July 2023; operationalizes updated NDC commitments for 2021-2030.
sources.methodology: Government plan operationalizing sectoral mitigation and adaptation actions under the 2021 NDC through an inclusive, multi-stakeholder process.
sources.limitations: The plan is a statement of intended actions; it notes that finances, technology, and human capital may constrain implementation.

sources.title: Sri Lanka, World Bank Sign Agreement to Strengthen Climate Resilience
sources.temporal_coverage: Press release dated 2021; includes projections through 2050 and a planned climate resilience project.
sources.methodology: Official World Bank release about a government program financing agreement and associated climate-risk estimates.
sources.limitations: The page summarizes estimates without their scenario/model specifications; project benefits are expected, not realized outcomes.

claims.locator: Environmental sustainability and climate change, printed p. 36 (PDF p. 36).
claims.paraphrase: The SCD reports 87 percent of the population lives in climate hotspots; floods and landslides mainly affect the Kelani basin, including Colombo, which accounts for about 40 percent of GDP.
claims.limitations: Figures summarize earlier studies.

claims.locator: Environmental sustainability and climate change, printed pp. 36-37 (PDF pp. 36-37).
claims.paraphrase: Estimated average annual disaster fiscal losses exceed US$380 million, of which floods account for about US$240 million.
claims.limitations: Annualized estimates in a 2022 diagnostic.

claims.locator: Poor households and climate risks, printed p. 37 (PDF p. 37).
claims.paraphrase: Poor households face disproportionate risks due to low assets, climate-sensitive livelihoods, residence near hazards, and limited safety nets and early warning.
claims.limitations: The factors are not separately quantified.

claims.locator: Water resources and climate risks, printed p. 37 (PDF p. 37).
claims.paraphrase: The SCD reports recent water shortages in Northern, North-Central, and Eastern Provinces; drought also threatens hydropower, which supplies about 30 percent of electricity capacity.
claims.limitations: Other water pressures also contribute.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed p. 1 (PDF p. 11).
claims.paraphrase: The plan says women and girls are less able to adapt to climate change and more likely to face disaster-related livelihood risks and losses; it also notes gender gaps in access to land, credit, technology, information, energy, water, social protection, and employment.
claims.limitations: This is the government's plan framing and does not quantify gender-differentiated impacts in the cited summary.

claims.locator: Executive Summary, printed pp. 1-2 (PDF pp. 11-12).
claims.paraphrase: The implementation plan covers nine adaptation sectors and states that finances, technology, and human capital may constrain delivery of its proposed actions.
claims.limitations: These are planned actions and identified implementation challenges, not a review of completed implementation.

claims.locator: Climate-risk estimates, webpage paragraphs dated 2021-09-20 (accessed 2026-10-26).
claims.paraphrase: The World Bank release reports a projected 1.2 percent annual GDP loss by 2050 due to climate change and estimates that nearly 19 million people may live in moderate or severe flood or drought hotspots by then.
claims.scenario: The press-release summary does not specify the model scenario underlying these estimates.
affected_groups: people in projected moderate or severe hotspots
claims.limitations: The official release does not disclose the assumptions or climate scenario for the summarized projections.

claims.locator: Project scope and Kelani basin measures, webpage paragraphs 113-124 (accessed 2026-10-26).
claims.paraphrase: The 2021 program was expected to benefit about 11.2 million people through upgraded weather, flood, and landslide forecasting and early warnings; planned measures include flood-resilient infrastructure in the Kelani basin and a salinity barrier at Ambathale for Colombo's water supply.
claims.limitations: The reported population is an expected project-beneficiary estimate and the measures are planned, not verified outcomes.

sources.title: Country Climate and Development Report: Western Balkans 6, Kosovo Country Compendium
sources.temporal_coverage: Country compendium dated October 2024; includes hazard history and climate projections.
sources.methodology: Country assessment combining climate and hazard exposure, socioeconomic vulnerability, adaptation analysis, and economic modeling.
sources.limitations: The report summarizes model outputs and cited hazard inventories; figures are not a new event-attribution study.

sources.title: Climate Change Strategy 2019-2028 and Action Plan on Climate Change 2019-2021
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment and Spatial Planning, Government of Kosovo
sources.temporal_coverage: Government strategy document dated 2018; action-plan period 2019-2021.
sources.methodology: Strategy developed by an inter-ministerial working group with expert support and stakeholder consultation, including a local questionnaire exercise.
sources.limitations: The inspected PDF is the 2018 strategy version and contains dated baseline data; it is not evidence of current implementation status.

sources.title: Kosovo's First and Voluntary Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.organization: Ministry of Environment, Spatial Planning and Infrastructure, Government of Kosovo
sources.temporal_coverage: Voluntary NDC adopted in 2025; mitigation targets extend to 2030 and adaptation sections describe current and prospective risks.
sources.methodology: Government submission synthesizing climate-risk evidence and proposed measures.
sources.limitations: Many measures are voluntary, conditional, and unfunded.

claims.locator: Adaptation risks, printed p. 9 (PDF p. 8) and section 2.1, printed p. 10 (PDF p. 21).
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR compendium reports frequent forest fires, floods, and landslides; 36.8 percent of Kosovo's area is at medium wildfire risk and 15.8 percent at high risk, with forests increasingly susceptible since 2000.
claims.limitations: The wildfire-risk percentages are spatial model classifications reported by the compendium, not measured fire losses.

claims.locator: Section 2.1, printed p. 10 (PDF p. 21).
claims.paraphrase: The compendium says mountainous areas face flash floods, including in the Drini basin where floods occur every two to three years; severe floods in 2013, 2014, and 2016 caused more than €4 million in estimated damage.
claims.limitations: Event dates and loss estimates are reported from the cited disaster inventory and source literature.

claims.locator: Executive summary, printed pp. 7-8 (PDF pp. 7-8).
claims.paraphrase: The government strategy identifies poverty, limited health and social-welfare services, illegal construction in hazard zones, inadequate water and sewage infrastructure, and weak municipal land-use planning as factors that heighten climate-hazard impacts.
claims.limitations: This 2018 strategy describes the government's contextual assessment at that time and is not a current service-capacity audit.

claims.locator: Climate hazards and drought impacts, printed pp. 58-59 (PDF pp. 64-68).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC reports drought losses above €50 million in 2009-2017, mainly crop failures; the 2022 drought affected agriculture across more than 10 percent of Kosovo's territory.
claims.limitations: Past losses are not all attributed to climate change.

claims.locator: Section 4.4 on women, children, and marginalised groups (PDF pp. 74-75).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC identifies disproportionate climate risks for women, children, and marginalised groups; women own 4.9 percent of farm land despite 49 percent of agricultural labor, while floods can disrupt children's education and services.
claims.limitations: NDC synthesis; no causal estimate.

claims.locator: Section 4.3.2.1, rural livelihood and resource-risk discussion (PDF p. 72).
claims.paraphrase: The NDC says drought, water stress, flooding, and weak farm adaptation could worsen livelihood threats and raise conflict or social-tension risks over natural-resource access.
claims.scenario: The cited NDC passage does not specify a climate scenario or dated horizon for this conflict-risk statement.
claims.limitations: Stated risk, not observed attribution.

sources.title: Updated Nationally Determined Contribution of the Kyrgyz Republic

sources.title: Lao PDR’s 2020 Updated and Enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical disaster impacts and national climate vulnerability described in the 2020 updated NDC submitted in May 2021.
sources.methodology: Government NDC synthesizing cited disaster assessments and regional climate projections.
sources.limitations: The NDC summarizes prior assessments and projections; underlying event and climate-model methods vary by citation.

claims.locator: Key findings, paragraph beginning “Laos has experienced rapid and unplanned urbanization…”
claims.paraphrase: The summary says unplanned urbanization heightens city climate risk; more frequent, intense floods could cause losses and damage critical infrastructure.
claims.scenario: The summary describes outcomes without preventive measures.
claims.limitations: The overview does not quantify city-level exposure, projected losses, or flood probabilities.

claims.locator: Key findings, paragraph beginning “Laos is water rich…”
claims.paraphrase: Climate change is increasing water-resource pressure, and hydropower is likely to be significantly affected.
claims.scenario: Scenario not specified in inspected passage.
claims.limitations: The summary provides no spatial estimates or hydropower projection assumptions.

claims.locator: Key findings, paragraph beginning “Agriculture faces considerable challenges…”
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR summary says climate change could harm rice cultivation and livestock, disproportionately affecting poor people and increasing farmers’ need for adaptation support.
claims.scenario: Scenario not specified in inspected passage.
claims.limitations: The overview gives no crop-specific impact magnitudes or subnational locations.

claims.locator: Priority action 10, paragraph beginning “Improve maintenance of roads…”
claims.paraphrase: The CCDR recommends road maintenance and expanded paving in high flood-risk provinces, prioritizing National Road 13 in Champassak.
claims.limitations: This is a report recommendation, not evidence that works occurred or outcomes were measured.

claims.locator: Section 3.1, “National context,” PDF p. 10.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC reports 2018 floods affected more than 600,000 people nationwide, with damage and losses estimated at US$371 million, or 2% of GDP.
claims.limitations: The NDC attributes figures to the government’s 2018 Post-Disaster Needs Assessment.

claims.locator: Section 3.1, “National context,” PDF p. 10.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC says tropical storms and depressions in 2019 affected more than 764,000 people across two central and four southern provinces, disrupting livelihoods and damaging property.
claims.limitations: The NDC cites a regional situation update; this passage gives no province names or sector loss totals.

claims.locator: Section 3.1, “National context,” PDF p. 10.
claims.paraphrase: The NDC expects warming across the Mekong region but says rainfall changes vary by location; altered temperature and precipitation may worsen flood conditions and affect crops, hydropower, roads, water supply, and food security.
claims.scenario: Scenario not specified in inspected passage.
claims.limitations: The NDC explicitly notes uncertainty in the magnitude and location of rainfall change.
